title: Macdonell and Allan's bridges environmental assessment
subtitle: Also: Baker Library lease referred, new external auditor, Brooklyn Park naming, and in-house utility billing.
overview: The Committee of the Whole spent most of its meeting on the Macdonell and Allan's Structures Environmental Assessment for the Speed River crossing downtown. It recommended approving the assessment and issuing the notice of completion {{vote:m8}}. That sets the overall plan: replace and widen the Macdonell bridge, build a new pedestrian and cycling bridge, remove Allan's Bridge, and rehabilitate the dam spillway. The committee also recommended keeping the bridge's railings for reuse {{vote:m9}} and consulting advisory committees on commemoration {{vote:m10}}. Staff will provide a memo on heritage review before Council considers the item.

The committee recommended appointing KPMG LLP as external auditor for 2025 through 2029 and naming the triangular park at Water, Albert and Martin streets Brooklyn Park. It referred the Baker Library lease to the October 28 Council meeting, with staff to report back on lease terms.

The committee received a report on moving utility billing in house, with the cutover set for the end of May 2026. A new customer accounts by-law is to come to Council in the first quarter of 2026. After closed session, the Mayor reported that Council gave staff direction on a parkland acquisition and was briefed on a new financial model for affordable housing on city-owned land. A report with the first two properties is due next month.

decisions.item: Macdonell and Allan's Structures Environmental Assessment
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the environmental assessment and directing staff to issue the Notice of Completion {{vote:m8}}.
The committee recommended that staff salvage and conserve the steel railing system and salvageable superstructure elements of Allan's Bridge for reuse near the site {{vote:m9}}.

The committee recommended that staff work with the Arts and Culture Advisory Committee and Heritage Advisory Committee on commemoration, placemaking and heritage conservation during design {{vote:m10}}.
The committee recommended appointing KPMG LLP as external auditor for fiscal years 2025 through 2029 and authorizing the Treasurer to sign the annual engagement letter {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended naming the triangular lot at Water, Albert and Martin streets Brooklyn Park, subject to a naming process review by the General Manager, Parks {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended approving the names proposed by the Naming Committee in the 2025 report {{vote:m3}}.
The committee referred the Baker Library lease item to the October 28 Council meeting without a recommendation, with staff to bring a memo {{vote:m6}}.
The committee received the report, and recommended a customer accounts by-law come to Council in Q1 2026 and an amendment to the Stormwater by-law on October 28 {{vote:m11}}.

debate: On the Baker Library lease, one councillor proposed a 40-year term with two 10-year renewals, or 30 years with two 15-year renewals, at the library board's discretion, for stability and fundraising. Staff said they preferred terms within a 30-to-50-year building lifecycle window. Other councillors wanted the board's formal input first, so the item was referred to Council with a staff memo to follow.

A delegate from a cycling advocacy group supported the new pedestrian bridge but asked that it be wide and well designed. The delegate also asked for cost detail on removing the dam to allow a trail underpass. Staff estimated at least $2 million for removal alone, with permitting and rail-bridge approvals possibly adding delay, and advised against deferral.

On Allan's Bridge, staff said rebuilding it for pedestrian use would replace everything but the railings, making it a replica rather than conserved heritage. Councillors asked whether a heritage impact assessment was required before the notice of completion. Staff said one will be done during detailed design and promised a memo on the process.

Some councillors questioned the cost and priority of the new pedestrian bridge when the widened Macdonell bridge will carry active transportation. Staff said the assessment must be approved as one solution, and timing and funding can be revisited in budgets. One councillor said they could not support the salvage clause.

On utility billing, councillors discussed property owners facing large unpaid water bills left by tenants. Staff said arrears can be moved to the property tax roll, as elsewhere in Ontario. Staff said the roughly $700,000 operating estimate stands, with postage as the main cost and e-billing planned for the new year.
